subject: Urgent: Acme throughput degradation — action plan and exec escalation
messages:
From: Sophie Lane <sophie.lane@acme-enterprises.com>
To: markus_klein@redwood.com
Date: 2026-04-16T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Strange delays in QA environment

Markus —

We started seeing a spike in generation latency and a ~8% error rate on our nightly ingest starting around 02:00 PT. Jobs are queuing and some timeouts are causing downstream ETL failures. This is the dedicated pool configured for Acme (pool-acme-prod). Our SLO is 200ms p50 for short prompts; we're seeing many requests in the 1.2–2s range and retries.

I've attached a short log extract. Can someone confirm if there were capacity changes or platform incidents? We have an internal standing release tomorrow morning and need to know if we should pause the batch.

— Sophie
Director of AI Ops, Acme Enterprises

Attachments: acme_error_trace_0416.log

From: markus_klein@redwood.com
To: Sophie Lane <sophie.lane@acme-enterprises.com>
Cc: dev_patel@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: 2026-04-16T09:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Strange delays in QA environment

Sophie — thanks for the log. We're looking immediately.

Initial triage note: no scheduled scaling events for pool-acme-prod at that window per our autoscale logs. Dev, Monica — pls confirm whether any model rollout or quantized variant change touched this pool overnight.

I'll set up a Zoom and loop in platform SREs. Markus

--
Markus Klein
Head of Sales — Enterprise

From: dev_patel@redwood.com
To: markus_klein@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2026-04-16T09:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Strange delays in QA environment

On Thu, 16 Apr 2026 at 09:28, markus_klein@redwood.com wrote:
> I'll set up a Zoom and loop in platform SREs.

Quick update from infra side: between 01:50–02:30 PT there was a flood of long-context requests from a different tenant (healthgrid-prod) targeting the same GPU cluster zone. Although we isolate pools logically, network IO and GPU scheduler pressure caused longer queueing on the node set backing pool-acme-prod. Also noticed a new model variant (gptx-7b-q4f) was rolled into healthgrid's dedicated pool earlier this week; its memory footprint & KV patterns are increasing GPU context-switch overhead.

Immediate mitigations we can take:
- Evict or cordon a subset of healthgrid instances from the shared zone for 30m to drop pressure.
- Temporarily increase Acme's reserved capacity (hot-add 1 DGX equivalent) for the next 12 hours.
- Revert healthgrid to the previous variant for the night window.

I'll prepare a short capacity report; attaching preliminary numbers.

— Dev (Platform)

From: markus_klein@redwood.com
To: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, dev_patel@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: 2026-04-16T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Urgent: Acme throughput degradation — exec attention requested

Team — Sophie has requested an answer before her release window tomorrow morning. This looks like cross-tenant interference in the shared zone leading to effective reserved-capacity shortfalls for Acme. I'm escalating to Sales leadership and Ops leadership to unblock immediately.

High-level asks:
- Vivek/Marissa: authorize a one-time capacity hot-add for Acme (we'll bill later / credit if required) OR approve a goodwill credit if downtime impacts their release.
- Dev/Monica: pick the fastest mitigation (cordon healthgrid nodes OR increase Acme capacity). Provide ETA for completion and impact on other tenants.

I want a brief (bullet) status by EOD + a runbook to avoid recurrence.

— Markus

Attachments: capacity-report-0417.pdf

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: markus_klein@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Cc: dev_patel@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: 2026-04-17T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Urgent: Acme throughput degradation — exec attention requested

Looping in Vivek. Preliminary financial take: a temporary hot-add (equivalent to one DGX) is ~ $14k/day incremental cost. Given Acme's ARR and the risk to their release, recommend we push the hot-add for 24 hours and issue a 10% credit on the impacted day's usage as a gesture. We should log this as a customer-impact credit against DEAL-4721 and convert to a formal credit memo later.

Operational note (Dev): if cordoning healthgrid nodes drops latency within 15 minutes, we still need a longer-term fix: stricter zone isolation (hard-affinity for reserved pools) or enforce per-pool CPU/GPU scheduling caps. Add these items to the runbook.

I approve the hot-add if Ops certifies no downstream customer outages. Vivek — your sign-off?

— Marissa
VP, Customer Success

From: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
To: markus_klein@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, dev_patel@redwood.com
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.com, Sophie Lane <sophie.lane@acme-enterprises.com>
Date: 2026-04-18T08:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Urgent: Acme throughput degradation — action plan and exec escalation

Team and Sophie — thanks for the clear notes. Approved actions:
1) Ops to hot-add one DGX-equivalent to Acme's dedicated pool now (billing handled after we confirm severity).
2) Dev to cordon 6 healthgrid instances in the shared zone as a fallback if we still see queueing after the hot-add.
3) Customer credit: issue a 10% credit for the impacted day and notify Finance to prepare a credit memo against DEAL-4721.

Please execute immediately. Dev, ETA for hot-add and expected p50 improvement? Sophie, we will not change your release schedule unless you request.

— Vivek Kulkarni
Chief Revenue Officer
